PARTIAL RESULT — the enrichment step is a hard environmental blocker; I could not determine the top GO:BP term.

What I executed (real, reproducible):
- DESeq2-style DE on the 6 target samples — combination arm = group "Cisplatin_IC50_CBD_IC50" (9_1,9_2,9_3) vs DMSO control = group "DMSO" (3_1,3_2,3_3) — using median-of-ratios size-factor normalization, NB-GLM log2FC (exact MLE), per-gene NB dispersions (method-of-moments) shrunk to a mean trend, Wald test, and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR.
- Result: 63,677 genes tested; 1,585 genes padj<0.05 (828 up / 757 down). log2FC range [-4.02, 3.71]. Top DE genes by padj: GDA (+1.27, padj 2.6e-183), ADGRF1, C1orf116, BTG2, STK17A, AEN, COL4A5, PCNA, FBXO22, ALS2CL, ZBTB20, ARID5B, VIPR1, PSTPIP2.
- Mapped ENSG→symbol (dropped 21,529 self-mapped/missing rows) and built the log2FC-ranked list of 42,148 real-symbol genes (39,258 unique) — this ranked Series is exactly the input the gseapy call consumes.

The blocker (STEP 4): gseapy.enrichr(gene_sets='GO_Biological_Process_2021', organism='Human', mode='both') CANNOT be run here because (1) gseapy is not installed and cannot be installed (environment is offline — no PyPI/DNS), (2) Enrichr (maayanlab.cloud) is unreachable, and (3) no local GO_Biological_Process_2021 GMT exists anywhere on the filesystem. Per your explicit instruction I am reporting this as a blocker and did NOT substitute a different gene-set library. Consequently I cannot report the top GO:BP term, its adjusted p-value, or the top-10 terms table — those require the blocked enrichment. I will not invent them.

The complete, correct pipeline script is saved as the artifact (analysis.py). It contains the exact approved gseapy.enrichr call; in an online/provisioned runner (gseapy installed + Enrichr reachable) it would produce the top GO:BP term and table from the same ranked list.
